---
title: "Data Mining"
---

This site is the hub for coding materials: [environment setup](/exercises/environment-setup-ko.html) and in-class labs.

This practicum is **data pattern mining**: frequent, sequential, structural, and relational patterns. The representation you choose (records, matrices, transactions, sequences, or graphs) determines which patterns you can find. Labs and homeworks implement that idea in Python.

::: {.callout-note}
## Konkuk eCampus

**Konkuk eCampus** is used for lecture slides, announcements, grades, and homework `.py` submissions.
:::

## Labs and Homeworks

**Labs** are for exploration. They are **not graded**. **Homeworks** are for evaluation.

### Labs (In-Class Exercises)

Labs go with each lecture unit. Setup, datasets, and a full lab list: [Exercises Guide](/exercises/index.html).

- **Lab 0 and Lab 1:** working code is provided. Run the cells and read the notes.
- **Lab 2:** implement the `TODO` functions in `lab02_*.py` first, restart the kernel, then run the matching notebook. On the course site, Practice outputs are the expected results after those functions are implemented.

Follow [Environment Setup (한)](/exercises/environment-setup-ko.html) or [Environment Setup (en)](/exercises/environment-setup-en.html). Start Jupyter from the repository root.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Always Run Cells Top to Bottom

If you skip cells or run them out of order, later cells fail (missing variables or imports). If something breaks, restart the kernel and re-run from the top.
:::

### Homeworks (Graded)

Graded work is the `.py` files in the schedule below. Submit them to eCampus. Other units will be posted later.

## Course Policies

### Autograder Rules

- **Do not change function signatures.** Keep names and parameters as given.
- **Do not modify docstrings.** The doctests inside them are used for grading.
- **Match the output format exactly.** Wrong type, wrong shape, or extra `print` statements fail the autograder even if the logic is right.
- **Use only the packages already imported.** Do not add extra `import` statements.

### Late Submission Policy

Late submissions are accepted up to 3 days after the deadline:

| Days Late | Penalty |
|:---|:---|
| 1 day | −20% |
| 2 days | −40% |
| 3 days | −60% |
| More than 3 days | No credit |

### Collaboration & Academic Integrity

The goal is that every student understands the material.

**Homeworks are individual.** Do not share code or written solutions, regardless of enrollment status.

**High-level discussion is welcome.** After at least 10 minutes on a problem yourself, you may talk it through or sketch on a whiteboard. Do not take away a written or electronic record: no notes, photos, code, or messages.

**On AI assistance.** You may use AI tools (ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, and similar) as a learning aid: to clarify concepts, read error messages, or check unfamiliar syntax. Two rules are fixed:

- **Understand what you submit.** You must be able to explain every line. If you cannot, that is an integrity violation, however the code was written.
- **Read the documentation yourself.** AI answers can be wrong or outdated. Navigating official docs (NumPy, pandas, Python) is part of the course. Treat AI as a starting point, not the final answer.
